messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@fintechco.com>

Cc: FinTechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — security items

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the product looked promising. A couple of security/compliance items we need to lock down before legal greenlights a POC:

- Current SOC 2 report (type II) + date of last audit.
- A list of subprocessors that will see customer data (cloud infra, monitoring, analytics).
- Clarify where tokenized PII is stored vs. processed (transient KV cache vs persistent storage).
- Any HIPAA controls if we enable PHI processing (BAA availability).

Can you share the subprocessor CSV and confirm whether Redwood uses any managed logs/monitoring third parties that receive unredacted request metadata? Also, if you have a short network boundary diagram, that would help our infra team.

Appreciate a concrete timeline — we aim to complete security sign-off by Oct 20.

Best,
Alex
Security Engineering
FinTechCo

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — security items

Alex — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick responses inline, and next steps below.

1) SOC 2: We completed a SOC 2 Type II in May 2027. I will attach the cover letter and the auditor contact in a secure link; for now, I can provide the summary and the date.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is a current exported CSV of our subprocessors + roles (compute, storage, monitoring, analytics). Highlights: AWS (us-west-2) for compute/storage, GCP (logging/analytics) for aggregated metrics, Datadog for runtime metrics (ingested as aggregated, no request bodies), and Cloudflare for CDN/edge routing.

3) Data routing & storage: By default, the runtime performs in-memory KV caching that is ephemeral and not written to disk. Long-term storage occurs only if the customer enables logs/retention or opts into usage analytics. We will mark these distinctions in the CSV.

4) HIPAA: We offer a BAA for customers that require it — we have a template and our legal team can engage if you need execution.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll drop the subprocessor CSV and a network boundary PNG by EOD (attached).
- Marissa will forward our SOC 2 summary and provide the auditor contact via a secure link.
- Neha will own the vendor questionnaire — can you send your standard security questionnaire to security@redwood.com?

If that timeline works, we should hit your Oct 20 target.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks — that sounds promising. Attaching our standard security questionnaire (vendor security questionnaire, ~50 Qs). A few clarifying items for your intake team so we can triage quickly:

- For Datadog: can you confirm whether request/response bodies are ever forwarded to Datadog logs (even in masked form)?
- For analytics pipelines (GCP): is any raw request metadata stored outside ephemeral caches?
- If customers enable 'full request logging', what retention controls exist and where is the data stored (region)?
- Is the KV cache encryption customer-keyed (bring-your-own-key) or platform-managed?

We've attached the SQ as FinTechCo_SQ_2027-10.docx. Can you aim to return a completed copy by Thu Oct 14? If not, a partial response with key documents (SOC 2, subprocessors, network diagram) will suffice to proceed to legal intake.

Regards,
Alex Grant
Security Engineer, FinTechCo

Attachments: FinTechCo_SQ_2027-10.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo security questionnaire & initial questions

Alex — thanks for the SQ. Quick answers to your bullets and where we added details in the attached doc: 

- Datadog: Redwood forwards only aggregated runtime metrics and numeric counters to Datadog. We do not forward request or response bodies. (See SQ section 7a for instrumentation details.)
- Analytics (GCP): Raw request metadata is not persisted in GCP analytics buckets by default. Aggregated telemetry (metrics and anonymized usage) may be stored for up to 90 days; raw inputs are ephemeral. (Details in redwood_subprocessors_2027-10-11.csv, column: storage_persistence)
- Full request logging: This is opt-in per-customer and requires explicit enabling in the Console. When enabled, logs are stored in the region selected by the customer; retention is configurable and subject to request-level redaction settings.
- KV cache encryption: Platform-managed keys by default (KMS). We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments — noted in the SOC 2 summary and the compliance addendum (see Drive link).

We've completed the attached questionnaire partially (answers to high-priority items) and flagged a few items for legal review. Neha will continue with the remaining sections and return the full SQ by Oct 14. If you prefer a DocuSign flow for the BAA, let us know and we can route it to your legal contacts.

Next steps:

- We will follow up with the auditor contact for SOC 2 evidence via secure portal link (Marissa)
- Neha to complete the remaining SQ responses by Oct 14
